hot.title: Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves
hot.summary: Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory researchers developed Self-Harness, a paradigm allowing a fixed Large Language Model (LLM) agent to autonomously improve its own operating harness by iteratively diagnosing weaknesses, proposing minimal modifications, and validating them. This method achieved significant performance improvements on the Terminal-Bench-2.0 benchmark across various LLMs, demonstrating the generation of targeted, model-specific harness configurations.

hot.title: Toward Generalist Autonomous Research via Hypothesis-Tree Refinement
hot.summary: An AI framework named Arbor enables autonomous research by organizing hypotheses, experimental evidence, and insights into a persistent tree structure. This approach allows agents to manage long-horizon scientific tasks and iteratively improve research artifacts more effectively than existing methods.

hot.title: First Steps Toward Automated AI Research
Breaking Entropy Bounds: Accelerating RL Training via MTP with Rejection Sampling
hot.summary: Bebop, developed by Alibaba's Qwen Team, accelerates large language model reinforcement learning training by enhancing Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) efficiency. It addresses MTP acceptance rate degradation by identifying target model entropy as the dominant factor and introduces an end-to-end Total Variation loss and a pre-RL adaptation strategy, achieving up to 1.8x end-to-end training acceleration.

hot.title: MiniMax Sparse Attention
hot.summary: MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) introduces an efficient blockwise sparse attention mechanism for large language models, enabling processing of ultra-long contexts up to 1 million tokens. The method achieves a 28.4x reduction in attention FLOPs and up to 14.2x inference speedup, while broadly maintaining model quality across diverse benchmarks.

hot.title: ICA Lens: Interpreting Language Models Without Training Another Dictionary
hot.summary: Researchers Sida Liu and Feijiang Han introduced ICALens, a workflow that makes Independent Component Analysis practical and efficient for interpreting large language model activations. The method recovers human-interpretable features with high non-Gaussianity and demonstrates competitive utility in sparse probing and targeted probe perturbation tasks compared to existing methods like PCA and some sparse autoencoder variants.

hot.title: Latent Spatial Memory for Video World Models
hot.summary: Mirage introduces a video world model that uses a latent spatial memory to generate 3D-consistent videos, achieving up to 10.57 times faster end-to-end generation and 55 times lower GPU memory usage compared to prior RGB-based memory approaches while enhancing geometric coherence.

hot.title: RLCSD: Reinforcement Learning with Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation
hot.summary: RLCSD (Reinforcement Learning with Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation) enhances the training of large reasoning models by mitigating "privilege-induced style drift" in on-policy self-distillation. The method achieves this by generating a contrastive, task-focused token-level learning signal that is robustly integrated with outcome-level rewards, leading to improved performance and stability on various reasoning tasks.

hot.title: From AGI to ASI
hot.summary: Researchers at Google DeepMind establish an analytical framework to map the potential evolution of artificial intelligence from AGI to ASI, outlining four technological pathways and six specific bottlenecks. The work provides a research agenda for predicting and managing the development of advanced AI capabilities.

hot.title: Test-Time Gradient Guidance of Flow Policies in Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: Researchers from UC Berkeley and Physical Intelligence introduce QGF (Q-Guided Flow), a reinforcement learning algorithm that achieves policy optimization entirely at test time. This method guides a pre-trained flow policy using gradients from a learned Q-function, demonstrating performance competitive with or superior to state-of-the-art training-time RL methods on continuous control tasks, while improving computational efficiency compared to Best-of-N sampling.

hot.title: InterleaveThinker: Reinforcing Agentic Interleaved Generation
hot.summary: A multi-agent framework called InterleaveThinker enables pre-trained image generators to perform long-horizon, interleaved text and image generation. This system addresses visual over-reliance and step-wise error accumulation, achieving performance on par with proprietary models like GPT-5-Thinking and significantly enhancing base models' reasoning abilities on benchmarks like WISE and RISE.

hot.title: Anatomy of Post-Training: Using Interpretability to Characterize Data and Shape the Learning Signal
hot.summary: Researchers at Goodfire developed a scalable, data-centric post-training pipeline that leverages interpretability tools, like Sparse Autoencoders, to characterize training data and precisely shape the learning signal for large language models. The framework demonstrates that interventions such as reward shaping can effectively mitigate undesirable behaviors and amplify desired ones, offering fine-grained control over model outputs.

hot.title: FlashMemory-DeepSeek-V4: Lightning Index Ultra-Long Context via Lookahead Sparse Attention
hot.summary: FlashMemory-DeepSeek-V4 implements Lookahead Sparse Attention (LSA) to dynamically manage the Key-Value cache, proactively fetching only query-critical historical chunks. This approach reduces the average GPU memory footprint by 86.5% while improving downstream accuracy by 0.6% on long-context benchmarks.

hot.title: MaxProof: Scaling Mathematical Proof with Generative-Verifier RL and Population-Level Test-Time Scaling
hot.summary: MiniMax developed MaxProof, a framework that significantly improves large language models' capabilities in generating competition-level mathematical proofs. This is achieved by integrating a multi-stage trained M3 model, which can generate, verify, and refine proofs, with a population-level test-time scaling method that iteratively evolves and selects solutions. MaxProof enabled the M3 model to surpass human gold-medal thresholds on IMO 2025 and USAMO 2026, boosting its one-shot scores by 8 and 10 points, respectively.

hot.title: Kwai Keye-VL-2.0 Technical Report
hot.summary: Kuaishou Group's Keye Team developed Kwai Keye-VL-2.0, an open-source Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) multimodal foundation model designed for understanding ultra-long video contexts and enhancing agentic intelligence. The model addresses extreme context scaling and catastrophic forgetting through sparse attention and multi-teacher distillation, achieving leading performance in temporal localization and strong results in various agent tasks.

hot.title: EurekAgent: Agent Environment Engineering is All You Need For Autonomous Scientific Discovery
hot.summary: EUREKAGENT demonstrates that carefully designing the operational environment for off-the-shelf LLM agents is crucial for reliable autonomous scientific discovery. The system achieved new state-of-the-art results in mathematical optimization problems and superior performance in kernel and machine learning engineering tasks while maintaining research integrity and cost efficiency.

hot.title: MaskWAM: Unifying Mask Prompting and Prediction for World-Action Models
hot.summary: MaskWAM introduces an end-to-end world-action model that enhances robotic control by integrating future mask prediction with visual prompting. The approach achieves improved policy generalization and resolves referential ambiguity by providing explicit semantic grounding and precise spatial anchoring across diverse manipulation tasks.

hot.title: i1: A Simple and Fully Open Recipe for Strong Text-to-Image Models
hot.summary: Princeton University researchers systematically investigated over 300 design choices for text-to-image models, leading to i1, a fully open-source model that outperforms previous fully open models by an average of 29.5 absolute percentage points and competes with larger open-weight models.

hot.title: World Tracing: Generative Pixel-Aligned Geometry Beyond the Visible
hot.summary: World Tracing, developed by World Labs and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, presents a generative pixel-aligned multilayer 3D geometry representation. It reconstructs visible surfaces and completes occluded 3D geometry from 2D inputs, showing improved accuracy on visible surfaces and comprehensive geometry generation for objects, scenes, and dynamic content while supporting various downstream 3D applications.

hot.title: Trajectory-Refined Distillation
hot.summary: Researchers at McGill University, Mila Quebec AI Institute, and UT Austin developed Trajectory-Refined Distillation (TRD) to mitigate 'prefix failure' in on-policy distillation for large language models. TRD refines student-generated trajectories, leading to consistent performance improvements, including up to +4.6% Avg@16 on AIME24 and +12.8% Pass@16 on AMOBench for specific Qwen3 models, while also generating substantially shorter, more verifiable reasoning paths.

likes.summary: ConMem presents a training-free framework for multi-agent systems to achieve continual adaptation by transforming fragmented experiences into structured, coordinated collective memory. It leverages signed strategy cards and a typed graph to provide prompt-side guidance, consistently yielding 10.9% to 12.9% absolute performance gains across diverse benchmarks and host LLM architectures.

likes.title: End-to-End Context Compression at Scale
likes.summary: Latent Context Language Models (LCLMs) offer an encoder-decoder framework for compressing large language model input contexts, enabling efficient handling of millions of tokens. This approach achieved up to an 8.8x faster Time To First Token and substantially reduced peak GPU memory compared to KV cache methods, while preserving high accuracy across diverse long-context tasks.

likes.title: Next Forcing: Causal World Modeling with Multi-Chunk Prediction
likes.summary: Next Forcing introduces a multi-chunk prediction framework to enhance causal world models by providing denser temporal supervision, addressing the issue of myopic supervision. It achieves new state-of-the-art performance on robot manipulation tasks, accelerates training by up to 2.3x, and enables 2x inference speedup while improving physical dynamics understanding and general video generation quality.

likes.title: AHA-WAM:Asynchronous Horizon-Adaptive World-Action Modeling with Observation-Guided Context Routing
likes.summary: AHA-WAM introduces an asynchronous, horizon-adaptive architecture for robot manipulation, decoupling the temporal scales of visual world planning and action execution. This approach achieves a 4.59x inference speedup and a 24.17 Hz control frequency (up to 56.95 Hz with distillation), while maintaining a 92.80% success rate on RoboTwin 2.0 tasks and 78.33% on real-world tasks.

likes.title: Echo-Memory: A Controlled Study of Memory in Action World Models
likes.summary: A controlled study by researchers from various institutions systematically compared different memory mechanisms in action world models, demonstrating that traditional replay metrics are insufficient for assessing a model's capacity to preserve consistent scene and object identity across camera revisits. The study revealed distinct performance trade-offs among memory families using a new three-branch evaluation protocol.

likes.title: MotionWAM: Towards Foundation World Action Models for Real-Time Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
likes.summary: A real-time World Action Model, MotionWAM, is introduced for humanoid robots, unifying whole-body control into a single motion latent space for complex loco-manipulation tasks. This approach achieved an overall success rate of 76.1% across nine real-world tasks, outperforming existing baselines by over 32% absolute gain and maintaining a closed-loop operating frequency of 4.9 Hz.

likes.title: OMG: Omni-Modal Motion Generation for Generalist Humanoid Control
likes.summary: Researchers at Tsinghua University developed OMG, an omni-modal motion generation framework, to enable generalist humanoid control by interpreting diverse human intents. The system leverages a large-scale, curated multi-modal motion corpus and a diffusion-based Motion Transformer, achieving real-time execution of complex, compositional commands on a physical Unitree G1 robot with high fidelity and stability.

likes.title: Rethinking the Divergence Regularization in LLM RL
likes.summary: DRPO introduces a novel regularization scheme for large language model reinforcement learning, integrating a divergence-based trust region with smooth quadratic regularization. This approach stabilizes training and improves efficiency, matching or surpassing existing ratio-based and hard-mask methods across diverse LLM architectures and precision environments.

likes.title: TRACE: A Unified Rollout Budget Allocation Framework for Efficient Agentic Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: A unified framework named TRACE was developed by researchers at Tsinghua University and Tencent to efficiently allocate rollout budgets in multi-turn agentic Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR). This framework improves learning signals by strategically exploring prompt roots and intermediate prefixes predicted to generate both successful and failed outcomes, resulting in consistent accuracy gains (e.g., 2.8 points on Multi-Hop QA) and a significantly increased proportion of informative training rollouts.
